regions.name: Anterior deltoid
regions.description: The front fibers help lift the arm forward and contribute to pressing movements.

exercises.name: Dumbbell overhead press
exercises.instructions: Start with dumbbells at shoulder height. Brace your trunk and press overhead through a comfortable range. Lower smoothly.
exercises.cue: Keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis.

exercises.name: Incline dumbbell press
exercises.instructions: Set a low incline, around 15–30°. Start with dumbbells beside your upper chest. Press upward and slightly inward, then lower with control.
exercises.cue: Keep your shoulders supported; avoid shrugging at the top.

regions.name: Middle deltoid
regions.description: The side fibers primarily lift the arm away from the body, as in lateral raises.

exercises.name: Dumbbell lateral raise
exercises.instructions: With elbows softly bent, lift the arms out and slightly forward to around shoulder height. Lower slowly.
exercises.cue: Lead with your elbows; avoid swinging your torso.

exercises.name: Dumbbell overhead press
exercises.instructions: Start with dumbbells at shoulder height. Brace your trunk and press overhead through a comfortable range. Lower smoothly.
exercises.cue: Keep your ribs stacked over your pelvis.

regions.name: Posterior deltoid
regions.description: The rear fibers move the arm backward and outward. Rows and reverse fly variations train this region.

exercises.name: Reverse fly
exercises.instructions: Hinge at the hips or support your chest on a bench. Open the arms outward with a slight elbow bend. Return slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep your neck relaxed and the load light enough to control.

exercises.name: Chest-supported row
exercises.instructions: Lie face down on an incline bench. Pull the dumbbells toward your ribs, then lower to a comfortable stretch.
exercises.cue: Let your shoulder blades move without lifting your chest.

regions.name: Supraspinatus
regions.description: Initiates and assists arm elevation while helping stabilize the shoulder joint.

exercises.name: Thumb-up scaption
exercises.instructions: With thumbs up, lift your arms slightly forward of your sides to a comfortable height, then lower slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep the weights light and avoid shrugging.

regions.name: Infraspinatus
regions.description: Externally rotates the upper arm and helps stabilize the shoulder.

exercises.name: Band external rotation
exercises.instructions: Keep your elbow bent at your side. Rotate your forearm outward against a light band, then return slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep the upper arm still and avoid turning your torso.

regions.name: Teres minor
regions.description: Assists external rotation and shoulder-joint stability.

exercises.name: Band external rotation
exercises.instructions: Keep your elbow bent at your side. Rotate your forearm outward against a light band, then return slowly.
exercises.cue: Keep the upper arm still and avoid turning your torso.

regions.name: Subscapularis
regions.description: Lies on the rib-facing surface of the shoulder blade and internally rotates the upper arm.

exercises.name: Band internal rotation
exercises.instructions: Stand beside an anchored band, elbow bent at your side. Bring your forearm toward your abdomen against the band. Return slowly.
exercises.cue: Use a comfortable range without letting your shoulder roll forward.

regions.name: Sternocleidomastoid
regions.description: Bends the neck and contributes to turning the head toward the opposite side.

exercises.name: Gentle neck-flexion isometric
exercises.instructions: Sit tall and place your palm against your forehead. Press lightly without moving your head, then relax.
exercises.cue: Breathe normally; do not use maximum effort or push into pain.

exercises.name: Gentle side-neck isometric
exercises.instructions: Place a palm above your ear. Press your head gently sideways into it without moving, then relax.
exercises.cue: Keep your head level and shoulders relaxed.

regions.name: Longus colli & longus capitis
regions.description: Deep anterior neck muscles support gentle nodding and cervical control.

exercises.name: Supported chin nod
exercises.instructions: Lie with your head comfortably supported. Make a small nod as if saying yes, then relax.
exercises.cue: Keep the head on the support and use gentle effort.

regions.name: Scalenes
regions.description: Assist neck side bending and stabilize or elevate the upper ribs.

exercises.name: Gentle side-neck isometric
exercises.instructions: Place a palm above your ear. Press your head gently sideways into it without moving, then relax.
exercises.cue: Keep your head level and shoulders relaxed.

regions.name: Splenius capitis & cervicis
regions.description: Posterior neck muscles that extend the head and help turn it to the same side.

exercises.name: Gentle neck-extension isometric
exercises.instructions: With head neutral, press lightly into a hand behind your head without moving. Relax between efforts.
exercises.cue: Avoid tipping the chin up or straining.

regions.name: Levator scapulae
regions.description: Connects the neck to the upper inner shoulder blade and elevates the scapula.

exercises.name: Dumbbell shrug
exercises.instructions: Stand with dumbbells at your sides. Raise your shoulders toward your ears, pause briefly, and lower with control.
exercises.cue: Keep your head neutral; avoid rolling your shoulders.

regions.name: Suboccipital muscles
regions.description: Small muscles below the skull fine-tune upper-neck extension and rotation.
regions.note: Use gentle shared loading; these small muscles are not isolated by the movement.

exercises.name: Gentle neck-extension isometric
exercises.instructions: With head neutral, press lightly into a hand behind your head without moving. Relax between efforts.
exercises.cue: Avoid tipping the chin up or straining.
